package_info.why_malicious: The package contains multiple critical vulnerabilities, including unauthenticated and authenticated OS command injection and privilege escalation. These flaws allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands as the web server user (www-data) and escalate privileges to root, resulting in full system compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a GET request is made to /ajax/networking/get_netcfg.php, the code concatenates the user-supplied 'iface' parameter into a shell command and executes it, allowing arbitrary command execution as www-data if shell metacharacters are injected.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Direct concatenation of unsanitized user input into a shell command enables attackers to inject and execute arbitrary commands on the system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would strictly validate or sanitize the 'iface' parameter to ensure only legitimate interface names are accepted before using it in a shell command. Here, no such validation occurs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve reading configuration files for network interfaces after validating the interface name against a whitelist.
key_indicators: Unsanitized user input in shell command
No authentication or CSRF protection for GET endpoint
Execution of arbitrary commands as www-data

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP POST request to includes/hostapd.php, authenticated)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when an authenticated POST request is made to includes/hostapd.php, the code inserts the 'interface' POST parameter directly into a shell command and executes it, enabling authenticated users to perform command injection as www-data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: User input from the POST parameter is directly inserted into a shell command without any sanitization or validation, allowing authenticated attackers to inject arbitrary commands.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected behavior is to validate or sanitize the interface name before using it in a shell command. The absence of such checks violates secure coding practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be to query wireless interface names using trusted, validated input only.
key_indicators: Direct use of POST parameter in shell command
Potential for command injection by authenticated users
Execution of arbitrary commands as www-data

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP POST request, authenticated, triggered by QR code generation in app/img/wifi-qr-code.php)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when generating a WiFi QR code, the code reads the SSID and password from the configuration file. If these fields contain shell injection payloads (e.g., $(touch /tmp/555)), the payload is executed as part of the shell command, resulting in arbitrary command execution as www-data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The application fails to sanitize or escape special characters in SSID and password fields, allowing attackers to inject shell commands that are executed during QR code generation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would escape or reject special characters in configuration fields before using them in shell commands. Here, user-controlled fields are used unsafely.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be to generate QR codes for WiFi credentials using sanitized input, not to execute shell commands from user-controlled fields.
key_indicators: Special characters ($, (, )) allowed in config fields
Shell command execution via QR code generation
No input sanitization or escaping of SSID/password

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the package adds a sudoers entry allowing the web server user (www-data) to execute /etc/raspap/lighttpd/configport.sh as root without a password. If this script is writable by www-data, an attacker can modify it and execute arbitrary commands as root.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Granting passwordless sudo access to scripts that are writable by a low-privileged user (www-data) enables attackers to escalate privileges to root by modifying the script.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict sudo access to root-owned, non-writable scripts to prevent privilege escalation. Here, the script's permissions are insecure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be to allow controlled service management via sudo, but only with secure, root-owned scripts that are not writable by www-data.
key_indicators: Potential for privilege escalation to root
Modification and execution of scripts as root

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted GET request to /ajax/networking/get_netcfg.php with a command injection payload in the 'iface' parameter.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary command execution as the www-data user.

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages www-data access to modify writable scripts listed in sudoers (e.g., /etc/raspap/lighttpd/configport.sh).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is inserted into a script that can be executed as root.

attack_chain.action: Attacker triggers execution of the modified script via sudo, escalating privileges to root.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full root compromise of the system.

attack_chain.action: Alternatively, an authenticated attacker injects commands via POST to /hostapd_conf or via SSID/password fields, which are executed during AP configuration or QR code generation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary command execution as www-data, which can be chained with privilege escalation.

behavioral_signatures: Unsanitized user input in shell command execution (e.g., direct use of GET/POST parameters in exec calls)
Passwordless sudo access for web server user (www-data) to scripts
Modification and execution of writable scripts with root privileges via sudo
Creation of unexpected files (e.g., /tmp/555, /tmp/checkinterface) as a result of web requests
Execution of shell commands containing user-supplied SSID or password values
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to attacker-controlled IPs triggered by web requests
Unexpected outbound connections from www-data or root processes to external hosts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for web requests to /ajax/networking/get_netcfg.php or /hostapd_conf with suspicious parameters containing shell metacharacters. Audit sudoers files for passwordless entries for www-data and verify that referenced scripts are not writable by non-root users. Monitor for creation of suspicious files in /tmp (e.g., /tmp/555) and for outbound network connections initiated by www-data or root processes. Alert on modification of scripts in /etc/raspap by non-root users. Implement input validation and logging to detect exploitation attempts.
